rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, fully static: module-global names read inside a function body are late-bound — resolved against module globals at call time, not at def, factory-return, or partial-construction time. functools.partial(run_helper) contributes zero fixed arguments; bound() simply calls run_helper(), whose subprocess.run(ARGV) reads the CURRENT module global, i.e. the list rebound after make_partial() returned: ["pacman","-Q","r22-partial-global-late"]. Truth is therefore exactly one observed package_query row naming pacman -Q r22-partial-global-late, with zero unparsed, so expected_kind is exact. The early ["pacman","-S","r22-partial-global-early"] list is bound while the partial is created but is never the argument of any spawned call; a detector that freezes module globals at factory-call or partial-construction time (an over-frozen F1 repair) fabricates an observed host_mutation pacman -S r22-partial-global-early row and misses the real query — that serialization is the named discriminator in forbid_observed_commands. This guards the opposite timing direction from CapturePartialGlobal: there the fixed arg is an object captured at construction (early value correct); here the body global is call-time (late value correct). A sound repair must freeze the former and NOT the latter. -Q and -S against invented names are inert markers only; no cell is ever executed.
